sanskrit: tasya jyātalanirghoṣaṃ droṇaḥ śuśrāva bhārata upetya cainam utthāya pariṣvajyedam abravīt
english: Droṇa heard the twang of his bowstring in the night, O Bharata; approaching him, he rose, embraced him, and spoke thus.

sanskrit: prayatiṣye tathā kartuṃ yathā nānyo dhanurdharaḥ tvatsamo bhavitā loke satyam etad bravīmi te
english: "I shall strive to make it so that no other archer in the world shall be your equal — this I tell you in truth."

sanskrit: tato droṇo 'rjunaṃ bhūyo ratheṣu ca gajeṣu ca aśveṣu bhūmāv api ca raṇaśikṣām aśikṣayat
english: Thereafter Droṇa further instructed Arjuna in the science of battle — on chariots, on elephants, on horses, and on foot.

sanskrit: gadāyuddhe 'sicaryāyāṃ tomaraprāsaśaktiṣu droṇaḥ saṃkīrṇayuddheṣu śikṣayām āsa pāṇḍavam
english: Droṇa trained the Pāṇḍava in mace-fighting, in swordsmanship, and in the use of the javelin, lance, and spear, as well as in mixed forms of combat.

sanskrit: tasya tat kauśalaṃ dṛṣṭvā dhanurvedajighṛkṣavaḥ rājāno rājaputrāś ca samājagmuḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: Witnessing his skill, kings and princes eager to acquire the science of archery came in their thousands.

sanskrit: tato niṣādarājasya hiraṇyadhanuṣaḥ sutaḥ ekalavyo mahārāja droṇam abhyājagāma ha
english: Then, O great king, the son of the Niṣāda king Hiranyadhanus — Ekalavya — also came to Droṇa.

sanskrit: na sa taṃ pratijagrāha naiṣādir iti cintayan śiṣyaṃ dhanuṣi dharmajñas teṣām evānvavekṣayā
english: The dharma-knowing Droṇa did not accept him, thinking "he is a Niṣāda," and out of regard for the welfare of his own students in archery.

sanskrit: sa tu droṇasya śirasā pādau gṛhya paraṃtapaḥ araṇyam anusaṃprāptaḥ kṛtvā droṇaṃ mahīmayam
english: That scorcher of foes then clasped Droṇa's feet with bowed head, entered the forest, and fashioned a clay image of Droṇa.

sanskrit: tasminn ācāryavṛttiṃ ca paramām āsthitas tadā iṣvastre yogam ātasthe paraṃ niyamam āsthitaḥ
english: Conducting himself toward that image as if toward his teacher, he applied himself with supreme discipline to the yoga of archery, following the strictest vows.

sanskrit: parayā śraddhayā yukto yogena parameṇa ca vimokṣādānasaṃdhāne laghutvaṃ param āpa saḥ
english: Endowed with supreme faith and supreme concentrated effort, he attained the highest swiftness in the release, receipt, and nocking of arrows.

sanskrit: atha droṇābhyanujñātāḥ kadā cit kurupāṇḍavāḥ rathair viniryayuḥ sarve mṛgayām arimardanāḥ
english: One day, with Droṇa's permission, all those crusher-of-enemies, the Kuru and Pāṇḍava princes, rode out in their chariots on a hunt.

sanskrit: tatropakaraṇaṃ gṛhya naraḥ kaś cid yadṛcchayā rājann anujagāmaikaḥ śvānam ādāya pāṇḍavān
english: O king, some servant happened to follow the Pāṇḍavas alone with the equipment, bringing with him a dog.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ vicaratāṃ tatra tat tat karma cikīrṣatām śvā caran sa vane mūḍho naiṣādiṃ prati jagmivān
english: As they roamed there seeking their various quarries, the dog, wandering foolishly through the forest, strayed toward the Niṣāda youth.

sanskrit: sa kṛṣṇaṃ maladigdhāṅgaṃ kṛṣṇājinadharaṃ vane naiṣādiṃ śvā samālakṣya bhaṣaṃs tasthau tadantike
english: The dog, catching sight of the Niṣāda in the forest — his limbs smeared with dark mud, wearing a dark deerskin — began barking and stood close by him.

sanskrit: tadā tasyātha bhaṣataḥ śunaḥ sapta śarān mukhe lāghavaṃ darśayann astre mumoca yugapad yathā
english: Then, displaying his lightness of hand in archery, he simultaneously shot seven arrows into the barking dog's mouth.

sanskrit: sa tu śvā śarapūrṇāsyaḥ pāṇḍavān ājagāma ha taṃ dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavā vīrā vismayaṃ paramaṃ yayuḥ
english: The dog, with its mouth filled with arrows, came back to the Pāṇḍavas; seeing it, the heroic Pāṇḍavas were filled with the greatest wonder.

sanskrit: lāghavaṃ śabdavedhitvaṃ dṛṣṭvā tat paramaṃ tadā prekṣya taṃ vrīḍitāś cāsan praśaśaṃsuś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Witnessing that supreme swiftness and the striking of a target by sound alone, they felt both ashamed and universally praised the feat.

sanskrit: taṃ tato 'nveṣamāṇās te vane vananivāsinam dadṛśuḥ pāṇḍavā rājann asyantam aniśaṃ śarān
english: Searching for him in the forest, O king, the Pāṇḍavas found that forest-dweller ceaselessly shooting arrows.

sanskrit: na cainam abhyajānaṃs te tadā vikṛtadarśanam athainaṃ paripapracchuḥ ko bhavān kasya vety uta
english: They did not recognise him, his appearance being so altered; then they asked him: "Who are you, and whose son?"

sanskrit: ekalavya uvāca niṣādādhipater vīrā hiraṇyadhanuṣaḥ sutam droṇaśiṣyaṃ ca māṃ vitta dhanurvedakṛtaśramam
english: Ekalavya said: "O heroes, know me as the son of the Niṣāda king Hiranyadhanus, a disciple of Droṇa who has laboured in the science of archery."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca te tam ājñāya tattvena punar āgamya pāṇḍavāḥ yathāvṛttaṃ ca te sarvaṃ droṇāyācakhyur adbhutam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having truly ascertained who he was, the Pāṇḍavas returned and reported everything that had happened — the whole wonderful occurrence — to Droṇa.

sanskrit: kaunteyas tv arjuno rājann ekalavyam anusmaran raho droṇaṃ samāgamya praṇayād idam abravīt
english: O king, the son of Kuntī, Arjuna, keeping Ekalavya in mind, privately approached Droṇa and said affectionately:

sanskrit: nanv ahaṃ parirabhyaikaḥ prītipūrvam idaṃ vacaḥ bhavatokto na me śiṣyas tvadviśiṣṭo bhaviṣyati
english: "Did you not embrace me alone and, with affection, declare: 'No disciple of mine shall surpass you'?"

sanskrit: atha kasmān madviśiṣṭo lokād api ca vīryavān asty anyo bhavataḥ śiṣyo niṣādādhipateḥ sutaḥ
english: "Then why does another disciple of yours exist who surpasses me and is mighty even by the world's reckoning — the son of the Niṣāda king?"

sanskrit: muhūrtam iva taṃ droṇaś cintayitvā viniścayam savyasācinam ādāya naiṣādiṃ prati jagmivān
english: Having deliberated and resolved for a brief moment, Droṇa took Savyasācin with him and went toward the Niṣāda youth.

sanskrit: dadarśa maladigdhāṅgaṃ jaṭilaṃ cīravāsasam ekalavyaṃ dhanuṣpāṇim asyantam aniśaṃ śarān
english: He saw Ekalavya — limbs smeared with mud, wearing matted hair and bark garments, bow in hand — ceaselessly shooting arrows.

sanskrit: ekalavyas tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā droṇam āyāntam antikāt abhigamyopasaṃgṛhya jagāma śirasā mahīm
english: Ekalavya, seeing Droṇa approaching near, went forward to meet him, clasped his feet, and touched the earth with his head.

sanskrit: pūjayitvā tato droṇaṃ vidhivat sa niṣādajaḥ nivedya śiṣyam ātmānaṃ tasthau prāñjalir agrataḥ
english: Having honoured Droṇa duly, the son of the Niṣāda, declaring himself a disciple, stood before him with palms joined.

sanskrit: tato droṇo 'bravīd rājann ekalavyam idaṃ vacaḥ yadi śiṣyo 'si me tūrṇaṃ vetanaṃ saṃpradīyatām
english: O king, Droṇa then said to Ekalavya: "If you are indeed my disciple, let my fee be paid at once."

sanskrit: ekalavyas tu tac chrutvā prīyamāṇo 'bravīd idam kiṃ prayacchāmi bhagavann ājñāpayatu māṃ guruḥ
english: Hearing this, Ekalavya replied with joy: "What shall I give, O venerable one? Let the teacher command me."

sanskrit: na hi kiṃ cid adeyaṃ me gurave brahmavittama tam abravīt tvayāṅguṣṭho dakṣiṇo dīyatāṃ mama
english: "For there is nothing I cannot give to my teacher" — and to him Droṇa said: "Let your right thumb be given to me."

sanskrit: ekalavyas tu tac chrutvā vaco droṇasya dāruṇam pratijñām ātmano rakṣan satye ca nirataḥ sadā
english: Ekalavya, having heard that terrible word of Droṇa, honouring his own vow and ever devoted to truth —

sanskrit: tathaiva hṛṣṭavadanas tathaivādīnamānasaḥ chittvāvicārya taṃ prādād droṇāyāṅguṣṭham ātmanaḥ
english: — with the same cheerful face and the same undepressed heart, cut off without hesitation and gave Droṇa his own thumb.

sanskrit: tataḥ paraṃ tu naiṣādir aṅgulībhir vyakarṣata na tathā sa tu śīghro 'bhūd yathā pūrvaṃ narādhipa
english: After that, the Niṣāda youth drew the bow with his remaining fingers, but he was no longer as swift as before, O lord of men.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaḥ prītamanā babhūva vigatajvaraḥ droṇaś ca satyavāg āsīn nānyo 'bhyabhavad arjunam
english: Thereupon Arjuna's heart was gladdened and his anxiety gone; and Droṇa was true to his word — no other surpassed Arjuna.

sanskrit: droṇasya tu tadā śiṣyau gadāyogyāṃ viśeṣataḥ duryodhanaś ca bhīmaś ca kurūṇām abhyagacchatām
english: Among Droṇa's disciples at that time, Duryodhana and Bhīma especially excelled in mace-fighting among the Kurus.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā rahasyeṣu sarveṣv abhyadhiko 'bhavat tathāti puruṣān anyān tsārukau yamajāv ubhau yudhiṣṭhiro rathaśreṣṭhaḥ sarvatra tu dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Aśvatthāmā surpassed all others in secret and esoteric knowledge; the twin sons of Mādrī exceeded other men similarly; Yudhiṣṭhira was foremost among chariot fighters; but Dhanañjaya was supreme in all respects.

sanskrit: prathitaḥ sāgarāntāyāṃ rathayūthapayūthapaḥ buddhiyogabalotsāhaiḥ sarvāstreṣu ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: That Pāṇḍava became famous to the ends of the sea as the leader of chariot-leaders, excelling in intellect, discipline, strength, and ardour, and in all weapons.

sanskrit: astre gurvanurāge ca viśiṣṭo 'bhavad arjunaḥ tulyeṣv astropadeśeṣu sauṣṭhavena ca vīryavān ekaḥ sarvakumārāṇāṃ babhūvātiratho 'rjunaḥ
english: Arjuna was distinguished in weapons and in affection for his teacher; though instruction in arms was equal for all, in grace and valour Arjuna alone among all the princes became an atiratha — a warrior beyond peers.

sanskrit: prāṇādhikaṃ bhīmasenaṃ kṛtavidyaṃ dhanaṃjayam dhārtarāṣṭrā durātmāno nāmṛṣyanta narādhipa
english: O lord of men, the evil-souled sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra could not tolerate Bhīmasena, dearer than life itself, nor the accomplished Dhanañjaya.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu sarvān samānīya sarvavidyāsu niṣṭhitān droṇaḥ praharaṇajñāne jijñāsuḥ puruṣarṣabha
english: Wishing to test all of them, who had completed every branch of learning, in the knowledge of striking, O bull among men, Droṇa assembled them all.

sanskrit: kṛtrimaṃ bhāsam āropya vṛkṣāgre śilpibhiḥ kṛtam avijñātaṃ kumārāṇāṃ lakṣyabhūtam upādiśat
english: He had craftsmen place an artificial bird made by artisans atop a tree, unknown to the princes, and set it as the target.

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca śīghraṃ bhavantaḥ sarve vai dhanūṃṣy ādāya satvarāḥ bhāsam etaṃ samuddiśya tiṣṭhantāṃ saṃhiteṣavaḥ
english: Droṇa said: "Quickly, all of you take your bows with haste; stand with arrows nocked, aiming at this bird."

sanskrit: madvākyasamakālaṃ ca śiro 'sya vinipātyatām ekaikaśo niyokṣyāmi tathā kuruta putrakāḥ
english: "The instant I give the word, let its head be struck off — I will engage you one by one; do so, my sons."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato yudhiṣṭhiraṃ pūrvam uvācāṅgirasāṃ varaḥ saṃdhatsva bāṇaṃ durdharṣa madvākyānte vimuñca ca
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The best of the Angirasa lineage then first addressed Yudhiṣṭhira: "O invincible one, nock your arrow and release it at the end of my word."

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiraḥ pūrvaṃ dhanur gṛhya mahāravam tasthau bhāsaṃ samuddiśya guruvākyapracoditaḥ
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, taking up his great bow first, stood aiming at the bird, spurred by his teacher's command.

sanskrit: tato vitatadhanvānaṃ droṇas taṃ kurunandanam sa muhūrtād uvācedaṃ vacanaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: After a moment, Droṇa spoke this word, O bull of the Bharatas, to that joy of the Kurus standing with bow drawn:

sanskrit: paśyasy enaṃ drumāgrasthaṃ bhāsaṃ naravarātmaja paśyāmīty evam ācāryaṃ pratyuvāca yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: "Do you see that bird perched at the treetop, O son of the best of men?" "I see it," Yudhiṣṭhira replied to his teacher.

sanskrit: sa muhūrtād iva punar droṇas taṃ pratyabhāṣata atha vṛkṣam imaṃ māṃ vā bhrātṝn vāpi prapaśyasi
english: After another moment Droṇa asked him again: "Do you see this tree, or me, or your brothers?"

sanskrit: tam uvāca sa kaunteyaḥ paśyāmy enaṃ vanaspatim bhavantaṃ ca tathā bhrātṝn bhāsaṃ ceti punaḥ punaḥ
english: The son of Kuntī replied to him: "I see this tree, and you, and my brothers, and the bird" — again and again.

sanskrit: tam uvācāpasarpeti droṇo 'prītamanā iva naitac chakyaṃ tvayā veddhuṃ lakṣyam ity eva kutsayan
english: Droṇa, as if displeased, told him to step aside, censuring him: "You are not capable of hitting this target."

sanskrit: tato duryodhanādīṃs tān dhārtarāṣṭrān mahāyaśāḥ tenaiva kramayogena jijñāsuḥ paryapṛcchata
english: Then the greatly renowned Droṇa, wishing to test them in the same order, questioned those sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra headed by Duryodhana.

sanskrit: anyāṃś ca śiṣyān bhīmādīn rājñaś caivānyadeśajān tathā ca sarve sarvaṃ tat paśyāma iti kutsitāḥ
english: And the other disciples — beginning with Bhīma — and the kings from other lands; all of them said "we see all of that" and were rebuked.

sanskrit: tato dhanaṃjayaṃ droṇaḥ smayamāno 'bhyabhāṣata tvayedānīṃ prahartavyam etal lakṣyaṃ niśamyatām
english: Then Droṇa, smiling, addressed Dhanañjaya: "Now you are to strike this target — listen well."

sanskrit: madvākyasamakālaṃ te moktavyo 'tra bhavec charaḥ vitatya kārmukaṃ putra tiṣṭha tāvan muhūrtakam
english: "The instant my word falls, the arrow is to be released. Draw your bow, my son, and wait just a moment."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ savyasācī maṇḍalīkṛtakārmukaḥ tasthau lakṣyaṃ samuddiśya guruvākyapracoditaḥ
english: So addressed, Savyasācin stood with his bow bent in a circle, aiming at the target, urged on by his teacher's word.

sanskrit: muhūrtād iva taṃ droṇas tathaiva samabhāṣata paśyasy enaṃ sthitaṃ bhāsaṃ drumaṃ mām api vety uta
english: After a moment Droṇa asked him in the same way: "Do you see that bird perched there, and the tree, and me?"

sanskrit: paśyāmy enaṃ bhāsam iti droṇaṃ pārtho 'bhyabhāṣata na tu vṛkṣaṃ bhavantaṃ vā paśyāmīti ca bhārata
english: "I see the bird" — so Pārtha replied to Droṇa — "but I do not see the tree, nor you, O Bharata."

sanskrit: tataḥ prītamanā droṇo muhūrtād iva taṃ punaḥ pratyabhāṣata durdharṣaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ ratharṣabham
english: Then Droṇa, with a gladdened heart, after a moment again addressed that invincible bull among the Pāṇḍava chariot warriors.

sanskrit: bhāsaṃ paśyasi yady enaṃ tathā brūhi punar vacaḥ śiraḥ paśyāmi bhāsasya na gātram iti so 'bravīt
english: "If you see the bird, tell me again." He replied: "I see the head of the bird — not its body."

sanskrit: arjunenaivam uktas tu droṇo hṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ muñcasvety abravīt pārthaṃ sa mumocāvicārayan
english: Hearing Arjuna say this, Droṇa felt his body hair rise with joy and said to Pārtha: "Release!" — and he released without hesitation.

sanskrit: tatas tasya nagasthasya kṣureṇa niśitena ha śira utkṛtya tarasā pātayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Then with a sharp razor-headed arrow, the Pāṇḍava swiftly cut off the head of that tree-perched bird and sent it falling.

sanskrit: tasmin karmaṇi saṃsiddhe paryaśvajata phalgunam mene ca drupadaṃ saṃkhye sānubandhaṃ parājitam
english: When that deed was accomplished, Droṇa embraced Phalguna and considered Drupada as already defeated in battle along with his allies.

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya saśiṣyo 'ṅgirasāṃ varaḥ jagāma gaṅgām abhito majjituṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Some time after, the best of the Angirasa line went with all his disciples to the Gaṅgā to bathe, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: avagāḍham atho droṇaṃ salile salilecaraḥ grāho jagrāha balavāñ jaṅghānte kālacoditaḥ
english: While Droṇa plunged into the water, a powerful aquatic creature — a crocodile — urged on by fate, seized him by the thigh.

sanskrit: sa samartho 'pi mokṣāya śiṣyān sarvān acodayat grāhaṃ hatvā mokṣayadhvaṃ mām iti tvarayann iva
english: Though capable of freeing himself, he urged all his disciples: "Kill the crocodile and free me!" — almost as if spurring them on as a test.

sanskrit: tadvākyasamakālaṃ tu bībhatsur niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ āvāpaiḥ pañcabhir grāhaṃ magnam ambhasy atāḍayat itare tu visaṃmūḍhās tatra tatra prapedire
english: At the very instant of his word, Bībhatsu (Arjuna) struck the submerged crocodile with five sharp arrows in quick succession, while the others were bewildered and scattered this way and that.

sanskrit: taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā kriyopetaṃ droṇo 'manyata pāṇḍavam viśiṣṭaṃ sarvaśiṣyebhyaḥ prītimāṃś cābhavat tadā
english: Seeing him so capable in action, Droṇa judged that Pāṇḍava superior to all his other disciples and was filled with joy.

sanskrit: sa pārthabāṇair bahudhā khaṇḍaśaḥ parikalpitaḥ grāhaḥ pañcatvam āpede jaṅghāṃ tyaktvā mahātmanaḥ
english: That crocodile, struck by Pārtha's arrows in many ways and cut to pieces, met its death, releasing the limb of the great-souled Droṇa.

sanskrit: athābravīn mahātmānaṃ bhāradvājo mahāratham gṛhāṇedaṃ mahābāho viśiṣṭam atidurdharam astraṃ brahmaśiro nāma saprayoganivartanam
english: Then the son of Bharadvaja said to that great-souled, mighty chariot warrior: "Receive this weapon, O mighty-armed one — the most excellent and supremely difficult to counter: named Brahmasira, complete with the method of its use and recall."

sanskrit: na ca te mānuṣeṣv etat prayoktavyaṃ kathaṃ cana jagad vinirdahed etad alpatejasi pātitam
english: "You must never employ this against human beings under any circumstance — if unleashed upon one of little power, it would incinerate the world."

sanskrit: asāmānyam idaṃ tāta lokeṣv astraṃ nigadyate tad dhārayethāḥ prayataḥ śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama
english: "This weapon, dear one, is called without equal in the worlds; keep it with the utmost care and with purity — hear this word of mine."

sanskrit: bādhetāmānuṣaḥ śatrur yadā tvāṃ vīra kaś cana tadvadhāya prayuñjīthās tadāstram idam āhave
english: "When some superhuman enemy oppresses you, O hero, you may use this weapon in battle to slay him then."

sanskrit: tatheti tat pratiśrutya bībhatsuḥ sa kṛtāñjaliḥ jagrāha paramāstraṃ tad āha cainaṃ punar guruḥ bhavitā tvatsamo nānyaḥ pumāṃl loke dhanurdharaḥ
english: "So be it" — having agreed, Bībhatsu with joined palms accepted that supreme weapon; and his teacher said to him again: "There shall be no other man in the world equal to you as an archer."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kṛtāstrān dhārtarāṣṭrāṃś ca pāṇḍuputrāṃś ca bhārata dṛṣṭvā droṇo 'bravīd rājan dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ janeśvaram
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having seen both the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and the sons of Pāṇḍu fully trained in arms, O Bharata, Droṇa spoke to king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of men.

sanskrit: kṛpasya somadattasya bāhlīkasya ca dhīmataḥ gāṅgeyasya ca sāṃnidhye vyāsasya vidurasya ca
english: In the presence of Kṛpa, Somadatta, the wise Bahlika, Gaṅgā's son Bhīṣma, Vyāsa, and Vidura —

sanskrit: rājan saṃprāptavidyās te kumarāḥ kurusattama te darśayeyuḥ svāṃ śikṣāṃ rājann anumate tava
english: — "O king, those princes have now fully acquired their learning, O best of Kurus; let them, with your permission, O king, display their training."

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn mahārājaḥ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā bhāradvāja mahat karma kṛtaṃ te dvijasattama
english: The great king then replied, his inner self filled with joy: "O son of Bharadvaja, a great deed has been accomplished by you, O best of twice-born."

sanskrit: yadā tu manyase kālaṃ yasmin deśe yathā yathā tathā tathā vidhānāya svayam ājñāpayasva mām
english: "Whenever you think the time is right, and in whatever place and in whatever manner — command me yourself to make the arrangements accordingly."

sanskrit: spṛhayāmy adya nirvedāt puruṣāṇāṃ sacakṣuṣām astrahetoḥ parākrāntān ye me drakṣyanti putrakān
english: "I am filled today with a longing, free from all despair, to see with my own eyes those sons of mine who have advanced through their mastery of arms — as others with eyes shall see them."
